chapters.title: A secret: the new meditation app

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: So we're going to start soon. And I'm going to tell you a secret. I don't know if I can tell you — I was going to ask teacher Tim if I could, and I forgot to ask. So don't tell him, okay, you people online. {? Broly}, you already know anyway. I don't know if he has talked about it. So don't tell — I'll ask him after the meditation.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: But V Houses has been working on their own app. Ah, cool — so I'm not that worried anymore. They already know, so that means people know. So I don't feel worried anymore.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: It is amazing. I fell in love with the app. I had Insight Timer — you know, the app for repetition — and I uninstalled it like three or four days after I got this. It is that good. Seriously, I don't switch apps that easily. And it's custom made for the lineage of Geshe Michael — custom made for Geshe Michael's practitioners.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: So you're going to get news about it soon. And that's what we're going to use today as well. And we're going to register our meditation stage — meditation stage, like the night stages. And in the end, we're going to check my stats, and we're going to realize that I don't pass from stage one.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: Okay, so get ready to meditate. Step number zero, the Buddha said: turn off the phone. Okay — alarms. What else? Notifications. Six Times Book notifications are also not allowed during meditation. Laptops in mute mode. And now we check our spine.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: We're going to settle in 10 seconds, and then we're going to hear a bell. And the reason it took me so long to give the introduction is because I wanted to talk as much as I can before we start — so when we're doing the meditation, we get quick instructions, and you spend less time listening to me and more time inside your mind.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: With our breath, we're going to do a hundred. Starting: exhale, then inhale — and that's round one, all the way to 100. If you hear me snoring, I'm chanting mantras, not sleeping.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: Okay, so here we go. Check your body, your posture. So now we do the breath.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: Observe your mind. And if it's agitated or dull, do the proper corrections. If your mind is dull, think of something bright. If it's agitated, think of something sad. And try to come back to your breath.

chapters.title: The meditation — bringing a teacher to mind

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: Now bring a teacher to your mind. And think about a quality that you really like about them. And truly admire that quality. Experience that respect that you feel towards them.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: Present them with a gift — something that you think they may like.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: And open your heart and confess to them something wrong that you did. Tell them how you regret it.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: And share with them something good you did — something you feel particularly happy about, that helps someone else. And look how happy they are — see how the other person is also very happy. Feel the joy building in your heart.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: Ask them to please keep teaching you. To guide you. To inspire you. And ask them to stay — to keep teaching you throughout your whole life. Let them know there's room in your heart for them, all the time.

chapters.title: The meditation — recalling a childhood teacher

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: And now go back to the time when you were six years old. And analyze all the teachers that you had in your life so far. It could be even your parents. Maybe a pet. A friend, a neighbor. A family member. A school teacher. Choose someone that taught you something that impacted your life till today. It could even be a grad-school teacher, or something.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: And think about the good thing that they taught you. Think about how that skill made the life that you have today possible. Contemplate. Feel the gratitude in your heart.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: Analyze how this teacher probably is not as normal as you think. Probably this teacher was something more than just a regular person who knew how your life would develop. Probably they would know exactly why you need to learn that skill.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: And see how that seed that created that teacher at that moment must have come from a previous life. Analyze how that seed was planted. Think about it. Don't — don't think that this story is crazy. Just let yourself go.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: Then go back to the moment when you were six, or the age you were when you met this teacher. And try to imagine how those mental seeds that you planted in that previous life are now projecting that teacher.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: And think about — just because you are projecting the teacher, it also may be possible for them to not be normal.

chapters.title: The meditation — bringing the teacher to your heart

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: Now come back to your body, right now. And the teacher that you picked for the first six preliminaries of the {? seven-limb offering} is right in front of you. And then they come to the top of your head. And then they face the same direction as you, and they shrink to the size of your thumbnail. And they sit on top of your head. And their body turns into light. And then they start to melt down — down through your spine, all the way to your heart. And they stay there to guide you throughout the day. And you feel safe. You feel motivated.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: Because that ray of light comes out of your chest and touches everybody in this world. That's the good seeds you planted during this meditation. And you give them all away. So they find a teacher. And they feel happy. And they get what they want. And you see them all smiling.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: So take three deep breaths — and I mean deep. Do not open your eyes yet. Just take those three deep breaths. Feel how your body and mind feel. When you're ready, you can open your eyes. Take a stretch. And relax.
